stem:
Deepak draws two straight lines that cross at one point. One of the four angles at the crossing measures 65°.

What is the measure of the angle vertically opposite that 65° angle?

options.text: 65°, because vertically opposite angles at the same intersection are equal.
115°, treating an adjacent angle on a straight line as if it were the vertically opposite angle.
65°, because the angles may be called opposite angles that must sum to 180°.
65°, only because 65 is already printed, without using the opposite-pair test.

teacher.key_rationale: At an intersection, vertically opposite (non-adjacent) angles are equal, so the opposite angle is also 65°. Using an adjacent supplementary angle omits the opposite-pair condition. Relabeling as opposite angles that sum to 180° substitutes a different relation. Echoing the printed 65 without the opposite-pair test is surface capture.
